c0628: Choose your legal structure: LLC vs S corp
c0631: The financial plan assumes an effective income tax rate of 25% (21% federal plus state), as for a C corporation. An LLC taxed as a pass-through pays through your personal return instead, and early losses carry forward as net operating losses. Compare an LLC vs S corp election with your CPA, using the plan's numbers.
c0632: Form the LLC with your state and get the EIN
c0635: Filing fees, annual reports and franchise taxes vary by state. Check your Secretary of State's website before you file.
c0639: State payroll and unemployment registration (and workers' comp insurance)
c0640: Premiums depend on your state, your payroll and your job classes. Get quotes from your insurance broker or the state fund.
c0641: Apply for the beer & wine license (state + local)
c0642: Start in week 1: ask your state alcohol beverage control (ABC) agency and your city what they need, and file as soon as you sign the lease (Phase 2). Sake usually falls under the wine license: ask your state ABC. Approval can take months; never open counting on it, and add liquor liability to your insurance.
c0643: Business bank account and business card
c0644: Keep them separate from personal accounts: card terminal settlements, delivery marketplace payouts and supplier payments all run through them.
c0645: Accountant / bookkeeper and a POS that reports sales tax
c0647: Payroll and onboarding for your team. Pick a POS that calculates and reports sales tax by jurisdiction before you buy it, and ask your CPA how often your state wants sales tax returns.
c0648: Take the plan to two SBA 7(a) lenders and compare loan offers
c0649: Bring the complete financial plan, with the month-by-month cash flow. Ask for quotes on equipment leasing for the walk-in cooler and the kitchen line, and ask each lender about the SBA Microloan (up to $50,000) as a complement. Lenders usually expect an owner equity injection (often around 10% for SBA start-ups; many want 20-30%).
c0666: Confirm the hood and duct route to the roof with your mechanical contractor
c0668: A dedicated, continuous, sealed duct to the roof, through a shaft or up an exterior wall, with the landlord's written approval if it crosses shared areas or the building exterior.
c0669: Negotiate the lease: free-rent period during build-out and security deposit
c0679: Zoning approval and certificate of occupancy
c0682: Building permit for the build-out and the hood
c0684: The build-out and the hood run through their own building permit and inspections: ask the building department which drawings and sign-offs they require.
c0702: Final inspections and certificate of occupancy
c0711: Submit your plans for health department plan review, apply for the health permit and book the pre-opening inspection
c0714: Submit the menu, equipment list, floor plan and finishes to your local health department for plan review (Food Code 8-201.11) before you build. After the final inspection you receive the health permit. Rules vary by state and county, so ask what they need.
c0740: Hot holding at 135 °F (57 °C) or above. Cool what you store with a written procedure that follows the Food Code cooling steps, and reheat to 165 °F (74 °C) within 2 hours. Log the temperatures.
c0741: Traceability and records: lots, temperatures and suppliers
c0749: Set pay rates against the state and local minimum wage and post the labor law posters
c0754: Offer letters for full-time and part-time staff
c0755: With schedule, pay rate and role. Collect a W-4 and an I-9 (with identity documents) from every hire, the I-9 within 3 business days of the start date. Classify people correctly: a 1099 contractor who works your schedule at your address is a misclassification risk.
c0758: Keep hours for every employee, part-time included (FLSA recordkeeping). A time clock in the POS makes it simple; agree with your CPA how to store the records.
c0762: Own delivery drivers: W-2 employees only
c0764: Your own drivers are employees on payroll (W-2), and because they drive their own cars on your behalf you also need hired and non-owned auto insurance (check your state). Do not treat them as independent contractors. Drivers for DoorDash, Uber Eats and Grubhub work for the marketplace, not for you.
c0769: OSHA basics: safety plan and training
c0772: Employee health policy and first aid
c0774: Have every new hire sign an employee health agreement (report illness symptoms; Food Code 2-201) and stock a first aid kit.
c0775: Allergen information on the menu or by staff script, with a written record
c0776: In writing on the menu or, if staff give it verbally, backed by a written record kept on site and a sign telling guests to ask. Keep one allergen matrix up to date for the whole menu.
c0803: Prices for the marketplace and for pickup at the restaurant
c0814: Background music: ASCAP, BMI and SESAC licenses
c0815: These are separate music licenses from performing-rights organizations, different from any city permit. Get all of them if you play music, or use a streaming service licensed for business.
c0818: Open in January, Month 1 of the plan
c0824: Trial services with the full menu
c0827: Check temperatures and records on day one
c0830: Health inspection: written food safety plan and records at hand

c0849: Compare actual sales and costs with the plan each month
